title: Why it was called sacko: the jai alai comparison
summary: Asked about the name, Green likens sacko to jai alai with no let-up and says it competed with the Three Rhythm Kings who became Tip, Tap and Toe.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: That's what I was trying to explain before, but I had to acquire popularity, see. The more you knew, the better you could be. See?
So, therefore, you were developing as you --
That's right.
-- as you were growing.
What were you and Chuck and Chuckles -- as Chuck and Chuckles doing?
Oh, well, we did our thing. We was doing the --
Did you try -- did you attempt to do some tacko?
Sacko?
Sacko.
(Laughter)
I done Yes, (unintelligible) tacko in.
(laughter)
I had that feeling. Did you attempt to do sacko or tacko?
I done tacko in, but I attempted to do sacko. She would -- she got in the show -- Kate Smith, you know. Now, you can imagine what that was.
What was the idea of calling it sacko? That's a funny name for a step.
Well, you haven't seen a game of jai alai --
how they play with this hand ball thing?
Yes.
Jai alai -- you see, that's saco, you know, no let-ups in it. See, it was a, you know --
Oh, you mean, the ball --
They could catch it like it's almost like throwing the ball, but they had something on one of their arms -- one of their hands, you know.
Who did?

The Jai alai player. See, that's like sacko, that's how -- I mean, it gets -- there was no let-up, it kept going -- getting thicker and thicker, see. That's how they did jazz tap dancing, see. The thing at the time was -- quit begging, you're old enough to steal, you see. See, they made pictures -- they was making pictures while they were doing this tap dancing, you know. A lot of suspense because you don't want to miss anything, see, they was actually trying to compare -- compete -- be competitive to what they call the Three Rhythm Kings, who eventually became Tip, Tap and Toe.
Ah.
See, they introduced the authority tap, see -- the Three Rhythm Kings, see. So, you have to get a picture, you know, photographically of their appearance. So, --
